title: Grade Control June 2026
body: When nobody's watching the block-by-block Balance row, ore gets left in the ground on a "Closed" block and nobody notices until the monthly SHG number comes up short. ADW has already lost 1,138t of SHG this way on a single block (770-160-177-1) — that's high-value feed written off because the closure call happened before the balance hit zero.
keyPoints: Read the Balance row first, not Total Mined. A negative waste balance means you over-dug against the model; a positive ore balance on a Closed block means gold got left behind.

Don't close a block just because mining activity stopped — check the balance is actually at or near zero, especially on SHG/HG bands where the tonnage per block is small enough that one short block moves the monthly number.
Grade bands (waste → SE → LG → MG → HG → SHG) reconcile directly against the daily report's feed-blend lines — use both together, not one in isolation, to catch a block that's under-delivering.
A run of negative waste balances across multiple closed blocks isn't noise — it's the block model under-calling waste, and that throws off strip-ratio assumptions in the weekly plan.
Track which blocks sit at zero with a full balance — that's your mining sequence made visible. It tells you where the fleet is heading next, not just where it's been.
apply: If a face goes quiet for several days on an open SHG/HG block, don't assume it's mined out — check whether it's simply unassigned (as happened when 770-160-177-2 sat idle nine days despite carrying an easily-closeable SHG balance) before you write it off.
